# Results — Study 481 (ZigZag Indicator)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **the ZigZag
identifies turns: when the indicator turns up off a swing low, that low was a tradable bottom** —
encoded as a mechanical rule with the **repaint removed**. A ZigZag swing low is only *confirmed*
once price has rebounded `pct = 5%` above it (the repaint lag); we read that confirmation on the
close of the confirmation bar and enter a long at the **next close** (one documented lag), then
measure the forward 5/10/20/60-day return. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (**total-return**) closes for **SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, GLD** (public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**As-of 2026-05-31**, partial June dropped; **21.4** years) |
| SPY fingerprint | `4cb5244f3990` (sha1[:12] of the close column, As-of slice) |
| Entries | **428** mechanical confirmed-up-legs (confirmed swing lows) pooled across the 5 tapes (`pct = 5%`) |
| Timing / costs | a swing low is usable only once price has rebounded **+5%** (the repaint/confirmation lag); enter the **next close** (one lag); hold 5/10/20/60 days; **1 bp** one-way × 2 legs per signal |

> **Price-only vs total-return.** The ETFs are auto-adjusted (dividends reinvested) — labelled
> total-return everywhere. The Signal axis uses a basket of **surviving** liquid ETFs; this is a
> single-instrument trend study, not a cross-sectional anomaly, so survivorship affects only the
> drift baseline (which is exactly what the random-entry control neutralizes).

## The signal — confirmed up-leg vs a drift-matched random baseline (the honest test)

One-sample *t* is the **misleading** number (it measures the index's upward drift); the
**Welch up-leg-vs-random** *t* is the test that matters. Δ = up-leg − random.

| horizon | n | up-leg | win% | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (up-leg−random) | net of cost | Welch *t* | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 428 | −5.9 bps  | 56% | −0.32 | +17.8 bps | **−23.7 bps** | −7.9 bps  | −1.04 | 0.298 |
| 10-day | 428 | +39.6 bps | 61% | +1.62 | +29.0 bps | **+10.6 bps** | +37.6 bps | +0.34 | 0.734 |
| 20-day | 428 | +111.9 bps | 64% | +2.87 | +53.4 bps | **+58.5 bps** | +109.9 bps | +1.33 | 0.183 |
| 60-day | 423 | +370.3 bps | 66% | +4.35 | +222.2 bps | **+148.1 bps** | +368.3 bps | +2.12 | 0.034 |

Read it carefully. The one-sample *t* against zero looks strong (**+2.87** at 20 days, **+4.35**
at 60) — but that is largely **beta**: long-only entries on an upward-drifting index inherit the
drift. Against the **drift-matched random baseline**, the confirmed up-leg is *worse* at 5 days
(Δ = −23.7 bps), a coin-flip at 10 days (Δ = +10.6 bps, *p* = 0.73), not significant at 20 days
(Welch *t* = +1.33, *p* = 0.18), and only edges over the *t* = 2 bar at the **60-day** horizon
(Welch *t* = +2.12, *p* = 0.034). Three of four horizons fail; the one that passes is the slow,
post-pullback drift — and the placebo below shows it is **not** the ZigZag's up/down geometry.

## Per-ticker (H = 20) — positive deltas, but no significant one-sample t

| ticker | entries | up-leg | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (up-leg−random) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 78 | +94.3 bps  | +0.98 | +58.9 bps | **+35.4 bps** |
| QQQ | 91 | +152.0 bps | +1.56 | +87.9 bps | **+64.1 bps** |
| IWM | 115 | +139.2 bps | +1.65 | +36.5 bps | **+102.7 bps** |
| DIA | 70 | +97.0 bps  | +1.25 | +50.6 bps | **+46.4 bps** |
| GLD | 74 | +52.9 bps  | +1.13 | +34.6 bps | **+18.3 bps** |

The 20-day deltas are positive in all five names — but **no per-ticker one-sample *t* clears 2**
(max +1.65 on IWM), the pooled 20-day Welch test is insignificant (*p* = 0.18), and the entire
effect is a slow drift after a pullback, not the up/down labelling (see the placebo). This is the
signature of relabelled, horizon-stretched beta — not a turn detector.

## Geometry placebo — relabel the legs, nothing changes

The decisive "does the up/down geometry matter?" test: keep the exact set of **confirmation
dates** and the price **marginal**, but on each draw randomise *which* confirmations are called
"lows" (the buy legs), matching the real count. This destroys the ZigZag's "up-leg = buy"
structure while keeping everything else.

| test | observed up-leg 20d return | placebo *p* | draws |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY relabelled-leg ZigZag | +94.3 bps | **0.645** | 500 |

**65% of relabelled-leg placebos match or beat the real up-leg** (*p* = 0.645). The ZigZag's
specific "this confirmation is a *low*, so buy" label carries no information — any confirmation
date does as well, because confirmation dates simply cluster after volatile pullbacks. "The
ZigZag identifies tradable turns" is busted.

## Synthetic positive control — the harness CAN bank a real turn

On a deterministic tape with a *planted* post-turn drift (knob `edge`: a real upward push for a
window of bars after each confirmed ZigZag low), the same confirmed-up-leg rule behaves exactly
as it must — so the flat real-tape result is a genuine "nothing there", not a dead detector.

| planted edge | n | up-leg | win% | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no planted turn) | 57 | −1.0 bps | 51% | −0.01 |
| **0.40** (real planted turn) | 52 | +435.0 bps | 81% | **+5.37** |

With no planted turn the control sits at *t* ≈ 0 (no false positive); a real planted post-turn
drift lights up at *t* = +5.37 with an 81% win-rate. The detector is live.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The confirmed up-leg does **not** beat a drift-matched random baseline at
  the horizons a "turn" signal lives on: Δ = −23.7 / +10.6 / +58.5 bps at 5/10/20 days with
  Welch *t* of −1.04 / +0.34 / +1.33 (all *p* > 0.18). Only the 60-day horizon clears *t* = 2
  (Welch *t* = +2.12, *p* = 0.034), and the placebo shows that is *not* the ZigZag's geometry.
  The strong one-sample *t*'s (20d +2.87, 60d +4.35) are mostly drift.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no residual turn edge once the drift is removed; the lone
  60-day blip is geometry-independent slow drift you capture more cheaply by holding the index,
  and costs only deepen the hole. No edge to scale.
- **"The ZigZag identifies tradable turns"? — BUSTED.** The relabelled-leg placebo leaves the
  result intact (*p* = 0.645): randomly chosen confirmation dates do as well as the real "lows",
  so the specific up/down structure carries no forecasting information. The ZigZag is a
  descriptive, **repainting** swing filter — strip the repaint and the turns stop being tradable.
